item.title: Trump reiterates that US attacks brought Iran back to 'the Stone Ages'
item.description:
After the Strike: How US Attacks Have Supposedly ‘Brutalized’ Iran

Donald Trump’s assessment of the US military’s impact on Iran has been stark. Speaking to Newsmax, the former US president claimed that his country’s strikes on the nation have brought Iran back to a state of “Stone Ages” technological prowess. According to Trump, Iran’s military capabilities have been severely curtailed, with 159 ships now lost at sea, a significant blow to the country’s naval power. Tehran’s air force, he asserted, has been decimated, with all aircraft either destroyed or rendered inoperable.

item.title: Israeli defense minister Katz says destruction in Gaza gives him a 'good feeling'
item.description:
Destructive Legacy in Gaza

The streets of northern Gaza, once bustling with life, now lie in ruins, a testament to the devastating effects of Israel’s military campaigns. Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz’s recent tour of the besieged enclave was met with a sense of pride, rather than remorse, as he described the widespread destruction as giving him a “good feeling”. His words, spoken with a sense of satisfaction, are a stark reminder of the human cost of the conflict.

item.title: US citizen found guilty of violating Iran sanctions
item.description:
A Guilty Verdict: US Citizen Convicted of Violating Iran Sanctions

In a high-stakes trial, a federal jury in Boston has convicted Mahdi Mohammad Sadeghi, a US citizen and Massachusetts resident, of violating US sanctions on Iran. The verdict marks a significant escalation in the ongoing tensions between the US and Iran, with far-reaching implications for international trade and diplomacy.

Sadeghi, a former employee of Analog Devices, was accused of conspiring to unlawfully export electronic components to Iran and of helping an Iranian business associate circumvent US export control laws in 2022. The alleged scheme involved the creation of a front company in Switzerland, which prosecutors claimed was used to evade US sanctions. After a trial that spanned several weeks, Sadeghi was found guilty on three of the five charges brought against him.

item.title: Trumps says he wants Gulf states to reimburse US for 'protection'
item.description:
The Gulf’s Bill: Trump’s Protection Racket

US President Donald Trump has sparked a firestorm in the Middle East by demanding that Gulf states reimburse Washington for “protection” provided by American military might. The bombshell announcement has sent shockwaves through the region, leaving many to wonder what this means for the delicate balance of power in the region.

At the heart of the controversy lies the Strait of Hormuz, a narrow waterway that connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and allows for the free flow of oil shipments. Trump claimed that the US has been providing protection to the Gulf states, citing Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar, Bahrain, and Kuwait as beneficiaries of this “protection.” The US president’s remarks were made in the Oval Office, where he stated, “I want to be reimbursed because we’re protecting a very rich portion of the world. We’re spending money, so… we are going to be reimbursed for protection.”

item.title: Nigeria: No Info About Our 78 Children Kidnapped By Boko Haram Weeks Ago, Parents Lament
item.description:
Desperate Pleas for Safe Return

In the scorching savannah of Borno State, Nigeria, a sense of foreboding hangs heavy in the air. Weeks have elapsed since 78 children, aged just 8 to 15, were abducted by Boko Haram terrorists from two local schools, Mussa Primary and Junior Secondary School, and Lassa Government Day Secondary School, in Askira-Uba local government area. Their parents, now a community united in anguish and desperation, have resorted to seeking divine intervention in the hopes of securing their children’s safe return.

item.title: South Africa: Do Not Take the Law Into Your Own Hands - IMC On Migration
item.description:
Vigilantism and the Rule of Law: A Delicate Balance in South Africa

The streets of South Africa have become a battleground for those pushing the boundaries of immigration law. While the government continues to grapple with the complexities of managing migration, isolated groups have taken it upon themselves to conduct identity checks on foreign nationals, igniting fears of vigilantism and the erosion of the rule of law.

The Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC) on Migration has sounded a stern warning to these groups, emphasizing that their actions are not only unlawful but also threaten the very fabric of South African society. Speaking at a media briefing in Pretoria, Justice Minister Mmamoloko Kubayi emphasized that the management of immigration, border management, deportation, and facilitated repatriation is the exclusive responsibility of the State. “Government reiterates that no individual or group has the authority to take the law into their own hands or to intimidate, threaten, or unlawfully remove any person from any community,” she stated firmly.

item.title: Moment of truth for Uhuru and Ruto in Sh7 trillion public debt suit
item.description:
Constitutional Contention

A judicial showdown is looming over Kenya’s leadership, as the government faces a constitutional challenge over its handling of the country’s Sh7 trillion public debt. The suit, filed by a coalition of opposition leaders, targets President Uhuru Kenyatta and his deputy William Ruto, accusing them of mismanaging the nation’s finances.

The stakes are high, with the court’s verdict set to have far-reaching implications for Kenya’s economic trajectory. The government has argued that a hearing on the constitutional challenge would undermine the appeal process, but the opposition remains resolute in its pursuit of accountability. The Supreme Court will now have to weigh the arguments presented by both parties, with a decision expected in the coming weeks.

item.title: Locations used as launch points for US attacks will be 'legitimate target', Iran says
item.description:
‘Legitimate Targets’ Emerge as Tensions Escalate: Iran’s Warning to Neighbours

In a stark warning to its neighbours, Iran has announced that locations used as launch points for US attacks will be considered legitimate targets. The statement, issued by Iran’s foreign ministry, comes as tensions between Tehran and Washington continue to simmer, just 25 days after a ceasefire agreement brought an end to the war.

The US has been accused of violating nearly all aspects of the ceasefire agreement, with Iran’s foreign ministry highlighting the country’s attacks on Iran’s transportation infrastructure, commercial shipping, cargo vessels, and aviation facilities. The ministry described these actions as among the gravest war crimes, a claim that has not been independently verified. Iran has long maintained that its military actions are defensive in nature, aimed at protecting its sovereignty and territorial integrity.

item.title: Two killed in mass shooting at Canada’s largest Latin street festival in Toronto, police say
item.description:
Chaos Erupts at Toronto’s Latin Street Festival

A scene of unmitigated terror unfolded on Saturday at Canada’s largest Latin street festival in Toronto, leaving two people dead and several others severely injured. As crowds of 13,000 people milled about, at least two shooters exchanged gunfire, sending festivalgoers into a desperate scramble for safety. The brazen act of violence has left the city reeling, with authorities scrambling to identify the perpetrators and restore order to the normally vibrant festival grounds.

item.title: Iran launched strikes on US military targets across the Gulf, Iran state media reports
item.description:
“Crossing the Red Line”

Sunday morning brought a dramatic escalation of tensions in the Gulf, as Iran launched a series of coordinated strikes against US military targets across the region. The attacks, which were widely reported by Iranian state media, marked a significant escalation in the long-simmering conflict between the two nations.

The strikes, which were launched in the early hours of Sunday morning, targeted several high-profile US military sites, including the Al Udeid Air Base in Qatar and the Port of Duqm in Oman. The Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) also claimed to have launched loitering drones against US military assets in Kuwait, including a Patriot air defense system. In Bahrain, home to the US 5th Fleet, Iranian forces claimed to have targeted a communications system and a radar installation belonging to US forces.

item.title: Iranian media says ship hit with missile after 'ignoring warnings'
item.description:
Strait of Hormuz Tensions Escalate as Iranian Media Reports Ship Hit with Missile

The fragile calm in the Middle East has been shattered once again, as reports emerge of a ship being hit with a cruise missile by Iranian authorities after allegedly ignoring warnings to turn back. The incident has sent shockwaves through the global trade community, particularly in the oil-rich regions of the Middle East, where the Strait of Hormuz has long been a crucial waterway.

item.title: UKMTO advises ships to transit with caution, report 'suspicious activity'
item.description:
Maritime Alert Issued After Iran Strikes Cyprus-Flagged Ship

In a tense escalation of the ongoing Middle East conflict, the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) has advised ships to exercise extreme caution when transiting through the Strait of Hormuz. The warning comes after an Iranian missile struck a Cyprus-flagged container ship, sparking a fresh round of US strikes on several Iranian cities.

The UKMTO’s alert is a stark reminder of the rapidly deteriorating security situation in the region. The organisation’s warning, issued on July 11, 2026, urges vessels to report any suspicious activity and exercise heightened vigilance when navigating the critical shipping lane. The alert was triggered by a report of an incident 9 nautical miles east of Oman, where a container ship sustained damage to its rear, causing a fire on board.

item.title: Group opposes alleged plan to cede Unity Schools to private investors, threatens lawsuit
item.description:
Unity Schools in Jeopardy: ASCSN Threatens Lawsuit Over Alleged Concession to Private Investors

The Association of Senior Civil Servants of Nigeria (ASCSN) has sounded the alarm over a reported plan to cede the country’s 120 Federal Government Colleges, popularly known as Unity Schools, to private investors. The move, if implemented, would have far-reaching consequences for the education sector, threatening the livelihoods of thousands of workers and the accessibility of quality education for children from low-income families.

item.title: Iran's Gharibabadi says 'UAE must be held accountable'
item.description:
‘A Scandal Document’: Iran Demands Accountability from UAE

In a scathing rebuke, Iran’s deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi has called for the United Arab Emirates (UAE) to be held accountable by the international community. The Iranian diplomat’s comments came in response to a recent announcement by the US Department of Commerce, which has eased export control regulations and elevated the UAE’s export status.

According to Gharibabadi, the document is a “scandal document” for Abu Dhabi, highlighting the UAE’s support for military aggression against Iran. In a post on X, Gharibabadi described the US move as “an official admission from Washington” that carries “direct international responsibility and legal consequences”. The Iranian diplomat’s words are a stark reminder of the escalating tensions between Iran and the UAE, which have been fueled by the latter’s increasing involvement in regional conflicts.

item.title: Turkish foreign minister calls for more pressure on Israel over Gaza aid
item.description:
Pressure is Mounting: Turkey’s Call for Increased International Aid to Gaza

In a stark rebuke of Israel’s handling of the ongoing humanitarian crisis in Gaza, Turkey’s Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan has urged the international community to step up pressure on the Israeli government to allow greater access to humanitarian aid for the besieged Palestinian territory. Fidan’s comments, made in an interview with The National, come as the international community grapples with the devastating consequences of the conflict in the Gulf and its own faltering attempts to broker a lasting peace in the Middle East.

item.title: Saudi Crown Prince and Trump discuss US-Iran talks, maritime security
item.description:
Regional Powerhouses Weigh in on Maritime Security and US-Iran Talks

As the complex web of international relations continues to shift in the Middle East, two of the region’s most influential figures have taken stock of the latest developments on the global stage. In a phone call, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and US President Donald Trump engaged in a wide-ranging conversation that touched on key issues, including US-Iran talks and maritime security. The Saudi Press Agency (SPA) has provided exclusive insight into the discussions, painting a picture of two leaders navigating the choppy waters of regional politics.

item.title: United Capital Group completes recapitalisation of SEC-regulated subsidiaries over a year ahead of deadline
item.description:
Capitalising on Compliance

The Nigerian financial landscape has undergone significant transformations in recent years, with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) at the forefront of these changes. The regulatory body has been instrumental in shaping the country’s financial sector, driving growth through rigorous oversight and enforcement. One entity that has demonstrated its commitment to this vision is the United Capital Group, a leading financial services conglomerate. In a major development, the company has completed the recapitalisation of its SEC-regulated subsidiaries, a feat achieved over a year ahead of the stipulated deadline.

item.title: West Africa: Mali - Guterres Calls for International Solutions to Curb Spread of Violent Extremism in the Sahel
item.description:
Sahelian Crossroads: Mali’s Battle Against Extremism

Maelstroms of gunfire erupt across the scorching desert landscape, as Mali’s fragile military falters against the relentless onslaught of extremist groups and northern separatist rebels. The very fabric of the nation trembles, as the Sahel’s fragile peace is torn asunder by the brutal forces of violence. Amidst this chaos, the international community has been urged to intervene, with UN Secretary-General António Guterres calling for a concerted effort to curb the spread of extremism across the region.

item.title: Russia’s Africa Corps describes Mali attacks as coup attempt, blames West
item.description:
Africa’s Complex Security Web Tightens Further

In the scorching desert sands of northern Mali, a brazen attack on a Russian private military company has sent shockwaves across the continent. As the world grapples with the implications of this bold strike, the Russia’s Africa Corps – a shadowy mercenary outfit with a reputation for operating in the continent’s most treacherous hotspots – has taken the extraordinary step of accusing Western powers of fomenting a coup attempt against the embattled Malian government.

item.title: Nigeria: Who Makes the Best Jollof Rice? King Charles Offers 'Diplomatic' Answer
item.description: As the soft glow of candelabras danced across the opulent dining hall, a subtle yet palpable sense of cultural exchange filled the air at the state banquet in Windsor, where King Charles III played host to a distinguished gathering of Nigerian dignitaries. With the weight of diplomatic propriety momentarily set aside, the British monarch endeavored to find common ground with his esteemed guests, and in doing so, he casually dropped a reference to a dish that has long been a staple of West African cuisine: Jollof Rice. The remark, though lighthearted in tone, served as a testament to the profound impact that Nigerians have had on various aspects of British society, from the culinary scene to the realms of politics, arts, and culture.

item.title: Missile fire kills three Palestinians in occupied West Bank
item.description: Violence has once again erupted in the occupied West Bank, leaving a trail of death and destruction in its wake. The latest incident, which occurred on Wednesday night, saw missile fragments strike a hair salon near Hebron, resulting in the loss of three lives and injuring 13 others. The victims, who included a teenager, were caught off guard by the sudden and devastating attack, which has sent shockwaves throughout the Palestinian community. As the people of the West Bank struggle to come to terms with this latest tragedy, questions are being raised about the circumstances surrounding the attack and the ongoing struggle for peace and security in the region.

item.title: Qatar contains two Ras Laffan fires, third still burning
item.description: Fierce blazes have ravaged the Ras Laffan Industrial Area in Qatar, with two of the three fires now under control, according to a statement released by the country’s interior ministry. The swift response by civil defence teams has been credited with containing the fires, preventing any reported injuries and potentially mitigating the damage to the industrial facilities. As the embers of the two extinguished fires continue to smoulder, attention has turned to the third fire, which remains active and poses a persistent threat to the area.

item.title: Ship struck by 'unknown projectile' near Qatar's Ras Laffan
item.description: Ras Laffan, a bustling industrial hub on Qatar’s northeastern coast, is abuzz with activity as the world’s energy giants converge to tap into the region’s vast natural gas reserves. But beneath the surface of this economic powerhouse, tensions are simmering, and the latest incident to rock the waters off Ras Laffan has sent shockwaves throughout the maritime community. A vessel operating in the area has been struck by an “unknown projectile,” sparking fears of a potential escalation in the region’s volatile security landscape.

item.title: Saudi analyst says kingdom will activate defence pact with Pakistan if it joins Iran war
item.description: As the conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran continues to escalate, the possibility of Saudi Arabia joining the fray has become a pressing concern for nations across the globe. The kingdom’s potential involvement in the war has significant implications, particularly in light of its mutual defence pact with Pakistan, which was signed last year. This agreement has raised eyebrows among geopolitical observers, as it could potentially draw Pakistan into the conflict and even put its nuclear arsenal on the table.

item.title: NSIA signs MoU with UK firm to develop dairy livestock platform in Nigeria
item.description: Dairy farming in Nigeria is on the cusp of a significant transformation, as the Nigeria Sovereign Investment Authority, NSIA, has signed a memorandum of understanding with a UK-based firm to develop a state-of-the-art dairy livestock platform in the country. This ambitious project has the potential to revolutionize the Nigerian dairy industry, which has long been plagued by low milk yields, limited access to quality feed, and inadequate infrastructure. The partnership is expected to bring in much-needed investment, expertise, and technology to boost the sector, with far-reaching implications for the country’s food security, economy, and employment landscape.

item.title: Sudan: RSF reportedly take over town near Chadian border
item.description: Sudan’s fragile security landscape has been further destabilized by the reported seizure of the border town of Al-Tina in North Darfur State by fighters from the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces. This development comes as fighting intensifies across the country’s west, raising concerns about the potential for regional instability and the impact on civilians. The images of RSF fighters celebrating their apparent victory, firing in the air and brandishing weapons, have sent shockwaves through the region, with many fearing the consequences of this escalation.

item.title: Israeli gas strike 'carried out with US support and approval'
item.description: As flames engulfed the largest natural gas site in Iran, a senior Israeli official revealed that the devastating attack was carried out with the full support and approval of the United States. This startling admission has sent shockwaves across the globe, exposing the intricate web of alliances and rivalries that shape the complex geopolitics of the Middle East. The Israeli official’s claim, corroborated by Israeli journalist Barak Ravid, has significant implications for the region, where the delicate balance of power is increasingly being tested by the actions of major world powers.
